upstream_authority.sampling_rule: all surviving particles are recorded on one explicit canonical-instrument-time grid until terminal loss or the declared archive horizon
upstream_authority.derived_handoff: a pulse-time handoff CSV is a materialized view of one archive time slice, never the sole upstream authority

execution_architecture.reuse_rule: downstream accelerator or TOF geometry, voltage, pulse timing or algorithm, and analysis changes reuse an unchanged verified upstream trajectory archive and materialize the required pulse-time slice
execution_architecture.invalidation_rule: a changed upstream source, multipole geometry, upstream field program, archive time grid or horizon, handoff plane, frame transform, or handoff state contract requires a new trajectory archive
execution_architecture.full_chain_policy: full multipole-to-detector runs are low-frequency handoff-equivalence validation only and are not the default design or optimization workflow
execution_architecture.rationale: separating component scopes makes accelerator and TOF iteration tractable while retaining one governed end-to-end equivalence check

identity_contract.lineage_policy: new products require a new particle_id, parent_particle_id and generation

timing_contract.solver_local_time_policy: local zero is allowed only when canonical instrument time is retained and restored

derived_solver_inputs.canonical_handoff_csv: authoritative transformed particle state and chain clock
derived_solver_inputs.row_map_csv: stable link between solver row order, particle identity and canonical time
derived_solver_inputs.metadata_json: input, contract and output SHA-256 plus transformation diagnostics
